Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of x about x=1.

a
1+12(x−1)2−564(x−1)4
b
1+12(x−1)−18(x−1)2+116(x−1)3−5128(x−1)4
c
1+12(x−1)−14(x−1)2+18(x−1)3−116(x−1)4
d
1−18(x−1)2+316(x−1)4
e
1+12(x−1)−18(x−1)2+116(x−1)3−364(x−1)4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by

P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=1, so

P4(x)=f(1)+f′(1)(x−1)+f″(1)2!(x−1)2+f‴(1)3!(x−1)3+f(4)(1)4!(x−1)4.

So we need to work out f(1), f′(1), f″(1), f‴(1) and f(4)(1), as follows: f(x)=x=x1/2⟹f(1)=1=1f′(x)=12x−1/2⟹f′(1)=12(1)−1/2=12f″(x)=−14x−3/2⟹f″(1)=−14(1)−3/2=−14f‴(x)=38x−5/2⟹f‴(1)=38(1)−5/2=38f(4)(x)=−1516x−7/2⟹f(4)(1)=−1516x−7/2=−1516

Therefore, P4(x) is given by

P4(x)=1+12(x−1)−14⋅12!(x−1)2+38⋅13!(x−1)3−1516⋅14!(x−1)4=1+12(x−1)−18(x−1)2+116(x−1)3−5128(x−1)4.
